  its white paint perpetually weathered by salt spray and
  Atlantic wind. Every evening, without exception, James
  climbed the 183 iron steps to the lamp room and lit the
  beacon that had guided mariners safely past the
  treacherous rocks below for over a century.
  His life was simple and ordered. He woke at dawn, made
  coffee, and scanned the horizon with his brass telescope.
  He maintained the Fresnel lens with meticulous care,
  polishing each prism until it gleamed. The machinery that
  rotated the light was older than he was, yet he kept it
